data.note:
Missed Eg5 inhibitors (AZ-C, BBBC021) as Microtubule stabilizers.

What misled me: well-average tubulin brightening (tub_mean z +16-28) plus microscopist language about "bundles in spread cells" at 0.003 uM. I treated that as interphase stabilization. In fact Eg5 inhibition produces monopolar spindles and prolonged mitotic arrest with condensed bright DNA and saturated tubulin in rounded cells — which raises well-average tubulin/DNA texture without true stabilization (PMID 19351824, PMID 31679979). Eg5/KIF11 regulation of mitotic arrest is established (PMID 28392145), and Eg5 binders are characterized biophysically (PMID 29162464).

Key ignored signal: atlas top-2 neighbors were both Eg5 (AZ138 sim 0.868, 0.866) with higher mean similarity for Eg5 (0.855) than stabilizers (0.828). I counted 6-vs-4 majority instead of weighting similarity rank. The mitotic proxy was unreliable at high dose yet I reused it to argue low mitotic fraction = interphase effect.

Lesson: require spindle morphology (monopolar vs bundled bipolar) at high resolution, not well-average tubulin intensity or low-mag "bundles," to separate Eg5 from stabilizers.

reflection.text:
The run correctly narrowed a strong antimitotic phenotype to microtubule/mitotic biology: 1 uM gave tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2 and tub_mean z=+28.5 with low solidity, low-dose 0.003 uM already showed tub_std z=+19.5, and the atlas returned only Microtubule stabilizers (6/10) and Eg5 inhibitors (4/10). Destabilizers, Aurora and DNA mechanisms were appropriately downweighted.
The error was interpreting whole-well tubulin brightening as interphase stabilization. Monopolar Eg5 spindles concentrate bright tubulin in rounded mitotics (PMID 31679979, PMID 19351824), which inflates the same well-average tub_mean/tub_std features, and Eg5 perturbation can co-alter tubulin staining (PMID 42392246). I ignored the review's quantitative warning that Eg5 had higher mean similarity (0.855 vs 0.828) and the top two neighbors, and I trusted frac_mitotic_like (rho=+0.80) even though it read only z+1.91 in the 1 uM replicate described as mitotically rich.
The acquisition plan reinforced this bias: repeat well-averages and two describe_phenotype calls that already favored stabilizers raised confidence 0.68 to 0.80 without the requested interphase-gated test of whether brightness was in spread interphase bundles versus confined to rounded mitotics. The needed discriminant was never measured at single-cell resolution.
what_was_right: Recognized potent antimitotic/microtubule phenotype from extreme tubulin z-scores and reduced density across 0.003-1 uM doses.
Correctly excluded microtubule destabilizers via positive tub_mean dose-response rho=+1.00 and retained Eg5 as second hypothesis from split atlas.
Flagged mitotic/DNA features (nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.8, low solidity, lower cell count) as consistent with mitotic arrest rather than non-mitotic MoAs.
what_was_wrong: Misread well-average tubulin brightening (e2, e8, e14) as interphase bundling without testing interphase versus mitotic confinement.
Dismissed compare_to_reference_atlas detail (e5): 4/10 Eg5 neighbors with higher mean similarity and top two hits over 6/10 stabilizer majority.

Overweighted unreliable frac_mitotic_like proxy (e10) after e14 showed it failed to report obvious mitotic enrichment at 1 uM, and escalated stabilizer probability on second describe_phenotype (e17) despite explicit Eg5 non-exclusion.

citations.claim: Eg5 inhibition produces monopolar spindles and suppresses proliferation, which can elevate mitotic tubulin signal.
Small-molecule Eg5 inhibition causes mitotic arrest and cancer cell death with reduced cell density.
Modulation of Eg5 can present with tubulin alterations and mitotic defects that mimic direct microtubule agents.

reflection.next_experiment: High-resolution alpha-tubulin plus DNA/pericentrin immunofluorescence gated by cell-cycle state: score monopolar versus bipolar spindles in mitotics and bundle frequency in spread interphase cells, with an Eg5 ATPase assay and cell-free tubulin polymerization control to separate Eg5 arrest from true stabilization.
